## Task
Parse the captured kubectl version output and validate it meets all acceptance criteria.

- Output contains "Client Version" section
- Output contains "Server Version" section (not connection errors)
- No authentication errors, certificate errors, or timeout messages
- Both versions contain major.minor version numbers
- All error patterns are absent

## Command
```bash
# Verify both client and server versions are present
if grep -q "Client Version" /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt && \
   grep -q "Server Version" /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt && \
   ! grep -qiE "error|certificate|unauthorized|timeout|refused|connection" /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt; then
  echo "SUCCESS: Both client and server versions present, no errors"
  echo "Client Version:"
  grep -A 5 "Client Version" /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt
  echo "Server Version:"
  grep -A 5 "Server Version" /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt
  exit 0
else
  echo "FAILURE: Missing version info or errors present"
  echo "Full output:"
  cat /tmp/kubectl-version-output.txt
  exit 1
fi
```

## Task
Test basic TCP connectivity to the cluster endpoint to verify the server is reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cluster endpoint hostname resolves in DNS
- TCP connection to the cluster endpoint succeeds (usually on port 443 or 6443)
- Connection timeout is reasonable (not hanging)

## Command
```bash
# Extract cluster endpoint from kubeconfig
CLUSTER_URL=$(kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig config view --raw -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}')
echo "Cluster endpoint: $CLUSTER_URL"

# Test connectivity (extract host and port)
HOST=$(echo $CLUSTER_URL | sed -e 's|https://||' -e 's|http://||' -e 's|:.*||')
PORT=$(echo $CLUSTER_URL | sed -e 's|https://.*:||' -e 's|http://.*:||' -e 's|.*/||')
if [ "$PORT" = "$CLUSTER_URL" ]; then PORT=443; fi

echo "Testing connectivity to $HOST:$PORT"
timeout 5 nc -zv $HOST $PORT
```

## Notes
This step verifies the cluster endpoint is reachable before attempting the full TLS handshake and authentication. If this fails, the issue is network/DNS, not auth.
issue.title: Test basic cluster connectivity

## Task
Parse the hostname from the cluster endpoint and verify it resolves in DNS.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Hostname is extracted from endpoint URL
- nslookup or host successfully resolves the hostname
- DNS resolution returns valid IP addresses

## Command
```bash
# Extract endpoint (reuse from child 1)
ENDPOINT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig config view --minify -o jsonpath="{.clusters[0].cluster.server}")

# Parse hostname
HOST=$(echo "$ENDPOINT" | sed -E "s|https?://([^:]+).*|\\1|" | cut -d: -f1)
echo "Testing DNS resolution for: $HOST"

# Test DNS resolution
if nslookup "$HOST" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  nslookup "$HOST"
  echo "SUCCESS: DNS resolution working"
elif host "$HOST" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  host "$HOST"
  echo "SUCCESS: DNS resolution working"
else
  echo "ERROR: DNS resolution failed"
  exit 1
fi
```
issue.title: Verify DNS resolution of cluster endpoint hostname

issue.description:
## Task
Verify that the cluster endpoint connection completes within an acceptable timeout threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Connection attempt completes within 10 seconds
- Timeout is properly enforced (does not hang indefinitely)
- Connection either succeeds or fails quickly with clear error

## Command
```bash
# Extract endpoint and parse hostname:port
ENDPOINT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}')
HOST=$(echo "$ENDPOINT" | sed -E 's|https?://([^:]+).*|\1|' | cut -d: -f1)
PORT=$(echo "$ENDPOINT" | sed -E 's|https?://[^:]+:([0-9]+).*|\1|')
echo "Testing connection timeout to $HOST:$PORT"

# Test with explicit timeout and timing
start=$(date +%s)
timeout 10 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$PORT" 2>&1
exit_code=$?
end=$(date +%s)
elapsed=$((end - start))

if [ $exit_code -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "SUCCESS: Connected in $elapsed seconds"
elif [ $elapsed -ge 10 ]; then

else
```

## Task
Verify that the cluster connection timeout is reasonable (< 10 seconds) and measure actual connection latency.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Connection completes within acceptable timeout
- Connection time is measured and reported
- Timeout value is verified to be < 10 seconds

## Command
```bash
# Extract endpoint
ENDPOINT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig config view --minify -o jsonpath="{.clusters[0].cluster.server")

# Parse hostname and port
HOST=$(echo "$ENDPOINT" | sed -E "s|https?://([^:]+).*|\\1|" | cut -d: -f1)
PORT=$(echo "$ENDPOINT" | sed -E "s|https?://[^:]+:([0-9]+).*|\\1|")

echo "Measuring connection time to $HOST:$PORT"

# Measure connection time with 10-second timeout
start_time=$(date +%s%N)
if timeout 10 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$PORT" 2>/dev/null; then
  end_time=$(date +%s%N)
  duration_ms=$(( (end_time - start_time) / 1000000 ))
  echo "SUCCESS: Connected in ${duration_ms}ms"
  
  if [ $duration_ms -lt 10000 ]; then
    echo "SUCCESS: Connection time is acceptable (< 10 seconds)"
    exit 0
  else
    echo "WARNING: Connection time exceeded 10 seconds"
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "FAILED: Connection timed out after 10 seconds"
  exit 1
fi
```

File: k8s/drawrace-build-workflowtemplate.yml, update-declarative-config step around lines 474-496.

2. The git push is anonymous https to git.ardenone.com, so it has no credentials and would 401 even without the stray line.

Fix both:
1. Remove the stray 'key: token' YAML fragment from inside the shell script
2. Wire authentication via a secret (see how docker-build wires github-webhook-secret as an example) and embed the token in the push URL

issue.description:
Plan ref: docs/plan/plan.md §Multiplayer & Backend 10 (Deployment) and §Testing 11 (CI Pipeline). File: k8s/drawrace-build-workflowtemplate.yml (in-repo copy of the iad-ci template; after fixing, sync to declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ via git commit+push — never kubectl apply directly).

Four concrete defects in the update-declarative-config template (around lines 474-496) plus the Kaniko step (~line 618):

1. Docker Hub org typo: line ~490 writes 'ronaldrayrun/drawrace-live:latest' into images.txt — should be 'ronaldraygun'. As-is it publishes a nonexistent image ref (ImagePullBackOff downstream).
2. Stray YAML fragment inside the shell script: lines ~495-496 end with 'git push' followed by an orphaned 'key: token' line INSIDE the block scalar — the shell executes 'key: token' as a command and the step exits nonzero. This is a remnant of missing secret env wiring: the git clone is anonymous https to git.ardenone.com, so the push has no credentials at all and would 401 even without the stray line. Wire a token from a secret (see how docker-build wires github-webhook-secret) and embed it in the push URL.
3. ':latest' everywhere: images.txt lines are fixed ':latest' strings, and the Kaniko docker-build template pushes only '--destination={{inputs.parameters.image}}:latest'. This violates the workspace convention 'never use :latest image tags' AND makes the bump a permanent no-op: images.txt content never changes between builds, so 'git diff --cached --quiet' always short-circuits the commit and ArgoCD never sees a new tag. Fix: push an immutable tag (git short SHA) from Kaniko and write the SHA-tagged refs into declarative-config.
4. Git identity: template commits as 'DrawRace CI <ci@drawrace.ardenone.com>' — convention requires user.name jedarden, user.email github@jedarden.com for all CI auto-bumps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Kaniko pushes ronaldraygun/drawrace-{api,validator,live} with a git-SHA tag (optionally also :latest, but manifests/images.txt must reference the SHA tag).
- update-declarative-config script is valid sh (no stray YAML lines), authenticates the push via a secret env, uses the jedarden git identity, and produces a real commit when the SHA changes.
- Org typo fixed (ronaldraygun).
- Repo copy k8s/drawrace-build-workflowtemplate.yml updated first, then the same content committed+pushed to declarative-config so ArgoCD syncs it (do not mutate the live cluster directly).
issue.title: Fix broken update-declarative-config step and :latest image tags in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate

issue.description:
The rotate-client-key step in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate runs kubectl using the pod's in-cluster SA token (iad-ci cluster), but tries to access drawrace namespace which doesn't exist on iad-ci.

The step is meant to update drawrace-client-key ConfigMap on iad-acb (the deployment target), not iad-ci.

Fix options (pick one):
A. Add a kubeconfig secret for iad-acb to argo-workflows namespace on iad-ci, then mount it in the rotate-client-key step and use KUBECONFIG env var.
B. Change rotate-client-key to commit the new key value to declarative-config (k8s/iad-acb/drawrace/api-deployment.yaml) and let ArgoCD propagate it — avoids needing cross-cluster kubectl in CI.
C. Use the existing iad-acb SA token (from iad-acb-readonly.kubeconfig) — create a new SA with write access to drawrace namespace, store its token as a secret in iago-workflows on iad-ci.

Option A is simplest. Steps:
1. Create a ServiceAccount in iad-acb/drawrace namespace with Role that allows get/apply on configmaps
2. Extract its token
3. Create a kubeconfig secret in iad-ci argo-workflows namespace pointing to iad-acb
4. Update the rotate-client-key template in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate to mount the secret and use KUBECONFIG

Note: this is P1 (not blocking pod startup, only HMAC key rotation on each deploy).

Acceptance: rotate-client-key node shows Succeeded in next drawrace-build run.
issue.title: Fix CI: rotate-client-key step targets wrong cluster (iad-ci instead of iad-acb)

issue.description:
Referenced in docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 (Consequences section, 2026-07-20).

Both the existing ?wheel= share link (apps/web/src/ResultScreen.tsx,
decoded in apps/web/src/App.tsx) and the planned ?ghost= link (see bead
"Implement shareable ghost-run links (?ghost=) per ADR-1") embed or imply a
PHYSICS_VERSION. If a link is opened on a build with a different
PHYSICS_VERSION than the one it was created with, replay/physics
determinism (the game's core invariant, per docs/plan/plan.md
"Deterministic Simulation") is not guaranteed to match.

Scope:
- On decoding a shared wheel/ghost, compare its embedded version (add one
  to the ?wheel= payload if not already present — currently
  encodeWheelForShare/decodeWheelFromShare in apps/web/src/ResultScreen.tsx
  carry no version field) against the running build's PHYSICS_VERSION
  (packages/engine-core/src/version.ts).
- On mismatch, show a short non-blocking notice: "this challenge was made
  with an older version of the game and may not replay exactly" rather
  than silently mis-simulating.
- Unit-testable: decode a payload with a bogus/old version and assert the
  notice fires.
issue.title: Add PHYSICS_VERSION mismatch guard for ?wheel=/?ghost= share links

issue.description:
Plan ref: docs/plan/plan.md §Multiplayer & Backend 6 (Matchmaking / seed pool) and Roadmap Risk Register row 'Matchmaking empty-bucket at launch — High likelihood'.

Tracks 2 and 3 shipped in the UI (apps/web/src/App.tsx TRACKS array: canyon-02 numeric_id 2, dunes-03 numeric_id 3; track JSONs at apps/web/public/tracks/canyon-02.json and dunes-03.json), but all ghost seeding is still hardcoded to track 1:
- seeds/ contains only track_1/ (25 blobs).
- crates/api/src/seed.rs load_seeds_if_empty() hardcodes /app/seeds/track_1 and a single TRACK_ID; s3_key format 'seeds/track_1/seed-NNN'.
- crates/validator/src/seed_loader.rs hardcodes seeds_dir.join("track_1").
- Every bundled ghost in apps/web/public/ghosts/*.json has trackId hills-01.

Consequence: matchmaking on canyon-02/dunes-03 returns empty buckets (nothing to race against) and offline players get no bundled ghosts for those tracks — exactly the empty-bucket risk the plan flags as High.

Acceptance criteria:
- 20-30 seed ghost blobs per new track committed under seeds/track_2/ and seeds/track_3/, generated with the existing tooling (crates/api/src/bin/generate-seed-ghosts.rs or scripts/generate-seed-ghosts.*) against the real track JSONs; each blob re-sims cleanly (finishes, passes validator structural checks).
- crates/api/src/seed.rs and crates/validator/src/seed_loader.rs iterate per-track seed directories instead of hardcoding track_1; per-track bucket distribution logic preserved.
- At least 3 bundled ghosts per track in apps/web/public/ghosts/ with correct trackId, each containing at least one mid-race wheel swap (plan Phase 1 deliverable pattern), and wired into the offline fallback used by App.tsx fetchGhosts.
- Unit tests cover per-track seed loading (extend the existing seeds tests in crates/api/src/seed.rs).
issue.title: Seed ghost pools and bundled ghosts for canyon-02 and dunes-03 tracks

issue.description:
Live-artifact review, 2026-07-20.

drawrace.pages.dev is a live, working PWA (confirmed 200 OK, ~150KB gz
bundle, verified rendering on a real Pixel 6 over ADB) with, as far as
could be found in this repo, zero usage telemetry. The plan's own Success
Metrics section (docs/plan/plan.md, end of "Roadmap & Delivery Plan")
defines D1 retention >=40%, median session >=3 runs, etc., but every one of
those is currently only measurable via the backend leaderboard's
player_uuid data — and the backend isn't deployed (see ADR-1 context).
Right now there is no way to know how many people are even visiting the
live site, completing the install flow, or finishing a race.

Scope:
- Add Cloudflare Web Analytics (free tier, no cookies, no PII, single
  <script> beacon or a Cloudflare Pages dashboard toggle — check whether
  it can be enabled purely from the Cloudflare Pages project settings
  without a code change first) to apps/web/index.html or via the Pages
  dashboard.
- This is orthogonal to and does not require the backend/leaderboard
  deployment work tracked elsewhere (bf-5ft/nd-xjnv/nd-639) — it measures
  the frontend that is already live today.
- Confirm it doesn't add measurable weight to the JS bundle budget (should
  be near-zero; Cloudflare's beacon is a separate small async script, not
  bundled into index-*.js).
issue.title: Add Cloudflare Web Analytics to the live PWA (zero backend, cookie-less)
